purpose: report/main.tex Future Work item 1 (as of the 2026-08-31 5th-review revision). Isolate whether the previously reported edge-attention refiner improvement is attributable to the edge prior specifically, or to added bottleneck attention capacity in general.
recipe: Identical to build_v51_edgeattnet_refiner.py (crop 320, context 1.65, 14 epochs, LR 2e-4 cosine annealing, AMP, crop-Dice-selected best checkpoint, fold-0 held out). Only the model class and seed vary.
provenance: Executed by the user in their own Colab session (colab-mcp bridge was disconnected for this run); output pasted back into chat verbatim and transcribed here. VERIFIED 2026-08-31 by reading the raw JSON directly from the mounted Google Drive (G:\\マイドライブ\\solar_filament_v30\\artifacts\\matched_param_ablation_fold0_manifest.json, saved alongside as matched_param_ablation_fold0_manifest_raw.json) and cross-checking against the executed Colab notebook's final cell output (Google Drive > Colab Notebooks > 'solar_filament_matched_param_ablation_colab (1).ipynb', execution_count 1-8, cell 7 has 181 outputs from the 6 training/eval runs) -- all values match exactly.
finding: Under a matched-parameter, two-seed comparison, the edge-attention variant's mean OOF PQ (0.440474) was not higher than either the plain U-Net baseline (0.441412) or the parameter-matched no-edge-prior attention variant (0.441259) -- it was in fact the lowest of the three, despite having the tightest seed-to-seed spread. This does not reproduce the originally reported fold-0 delta of +0.0062 (plain 0.4393 -> edge-attention 0.4454) that was one basis for accepting the edge-attention refiner as a validated improvement.
caveats: n=2 seeds per variant, fold 0 only. Not a substitute for the full bootstrap/multi-fold protocol used elsewhere in this project; treated as a strong but not yet conclusive signal pending more seeds and folds 1-2 (see report/main.tex Future Work).
